Dataset name: Manitoba Longitudinal Study of Young Adults
Owner / data controller: GREO/Borealis repository
Access type: Repository access
Gambling measure summary: PGSI and Canadian Problem Gambling Index (CPGI) problem-gambling severity, Gambling Motives Questionnaire (GMQ), and gambling-cognition measures (Beliefs About Randomness; Drake Beliefs About Chance Inventory) across four annual waves (2007-2011). Variable names from public MLSYA codebook.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Substance use (Alcohol/Drug Dependence Scales), mental health (CIDI, Rosenberg, SF-8), impulsivity/personality (BIS-11, NEO-FFI), social support (MSPSS), coping and spirituality (Ways of Coping; SIBS-R), life events. From public MLSYA codebook.
Notes / uncertainties: Potentially useful for gambling, psychosocial and substance-use risk/protective factors.
Sampling design: Longitudinal community sample of young adults in Manitoba
Data collection mode: Interviewer-administered and self-completion questionnaires

Dataset name: British Gambling Prevalence Survey

Gambling measure summary: Gambling participation, frequency, mode, volume; problem gambling screens in documentation to verify
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Demographics, health/substance and socioeconomic factors depending year
Notes / uncertainties: Useful for trend/older 16-24 analyses; age and measures comparable to later adult surveys to assess
Sampling design: Stratified random probability sample of adults in private households
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview plus self-completion for the gambling questions

Dataset name: Health Survey for England

Access type: UKDS registered access

Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Physical/mental health, alcohol, smoking, BMI, socioeconomic and inequality variables
Notes / uncertainties: Strong health/risk-factor data; gambling modules included in 2012, 2015, 2016, 2018, 2021. Harmonisation across years needs care.
Linkage: HES and mortality records via NHS England (approval needed)
Sampling design: Stratified multistage random probability sample of addresses
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview (CAPI) plus self-completion for the gambling module

Dataset name: Gambling in England and Scotland, 2016: Combined HSE/SHeS
Owner / data controller: NHS Digital / Scottish Government / NatCen; UKDS
Access type: UKDS registered access
Gambling measure summary: Past-year participation across 19 gambling activities (National Lottery, scratchcards, bingo, machines, casino, online gambling/betting, sports/horse/dog betting, spread betting, private betting), plus full problem-gambling screens: the PGSI (9 items + score/bands) and DSM-IV problem gambling (10 items + score), with combined problem-gambling derivations. Variable names and labels from the official UKDS SN 8416 variable list.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental health and wellbeing (WEMWBS, GHQ-12), substance use (smoking and alcohol consumption), physical health (longstanding illness, conditions, BMI/anthropometry), and socioeconomic and demographic factors (income, NS-SEC, education, employment, tenure, ethnicity). From the official UKDS SN 8416 variable list.
Notes / uncertainties: Useful harmonised England/Scotland comparator
Sampling design: Random probability household samples (HSE and SHeS gambling data combined)
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview plus self-completion for the gambling module

Dataset name: National Survey for Wales gambling module
Owner / data controller: Welsh Government; UKDS

Access type: UKDS registered access
Gambling measure summary: Gambling activity/behaviours in previous 12 months; measure details to extract from data dictionary
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Demographics, deprivation, wellbeing, health, household and area variables
Notes / uncertainties: Under-25 subsample likely small; variable-level detail pending

Dataset name: Growing Up in Ireland Cohort '98
Owner / data controller: Economic and Social Research Institute / Irish Social Sciences Data Archive
Age focus / population: Longitudinal cohort; gambling questions at age 20 (Wave 4) only
Access type: ISSDA application / data request
Gambling measure summary: Brief 3-item gambling participation/frequency module at age 20 (Wave 4): lottery/scratchcards, casino tables/slot machines/video poker, and other betting (cards, bingo, horse/sports betting), each on a 6-point frequency scale (in person or online). Wording from the public Young Person questionnaire. NOTE: gambling items are excluded from the public AMF microdata - the analysis-ready variables require the Researcher Microdata File (RMF) via the CSO. No gambling items at 17/18.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental health/wellbeing (e.g. CES-D/DASS components), socioeconomic, family, education, health behaviours
Notes / uncertainties: Verified 2026-06-15: gambling is a 3-item module at age 20 only (not 17/18). Gambling variables are not in the released AMF; RMF (CSO Officer of Statistics) needed for data. Useful as a youth participation comparator but not for problem-gambling harmonisation.
Sampling design: Nationally representative sample recruited through the primary school system
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview (CAPI) plus self-completion for sensitive items

Dataset name: Gambling Impact and Behavior Study
Owner / data controller: National Opinion Research Center / ICPSR NAHDAP
Study design: Cross-sectional adult and youth survey plus community files
Age focus / population: Adults and youth in the US; youth sample includes adolescents
Access type: ICPSR/NAHDAP access
Gambling measure summary: Youth survey (16-17): past-year and lifetime gambling participation and spend across many activities (lottery, scratchcards, casino games, bingo, private games, store/bar machines, unlicensed gambling), reasons/motivations for gambling, favourite activities, and full problem gambling assessment via the NODS (NORC DSM-IV Screen) - 10 DSM-IV criteria lifetime and past-12-months with derived 0-10 scores. From the official ICPSR 2778 Youth Survey codebook.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Substance use (alcohol, marijuana, cocaine, stimulants, tranquillisers - use, consequences and dependence), mental health and wellbeing (depression episodes, mental-health treatment), physical health, family and household circumstances, legal/adversity, religiosity, and socioeconomic and demographic factors. From the official ICPSR 2778 Youth Survey codebook.
Notes / uncertainties: Historical US comparator; less relevant for current digital gambling
Sampling design: Random digit dialling telephone sample plus a gambling-venue patron survey
Data collection mode: Telephone interview plus in-person patron survey

Dataset name: Scottish Health Survey 2012-2017 and 2021 (gambling module years)
Owner / data controller: Scottish Government / ScotCen / UK Data Service
Access type: Safeguarded/End User Licence raw data; public metadata in uploaded dictionary
Gambling measure summary: Gambling module included in SHeS 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, and 2021. Measures include PGSI (9 items, score 0-27) and DSM-IV problem gambling screen (10 items), both included since 2012. Past-year gambling participation items also included. The gambling module has been dropped from future SHeS waves as the Gambling Survey for Great Britain now covers Scottish adults annually.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental health/wellbeing (WEMWBS, GHQ-12), substance use (smoking, alcohol), socioeconomic position/inequalities, family/household, digital environment, diet/physical health.
Notes / uncertainties: SHeS runs annually 1995-2024 but gambling questions only asked in 2012-2017 and 2021. The 2018 and 2019 survey years did not include the gambling module. Uploaded data dictionary covers 2017/2018/2019/2021 combined file (shes17181921i_eul; 1780 variables; 25128 cases) but gambling variables are only present for 2017 and 2021 within that file.
Linkage: Hospital records (SMR) and mortality via eDRIS
Sampling design: Stratified random probability sample of addresses in Scotland
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview (CAPI) plus self-completion for the gambling module

Dataset name: Access to Healthy Assets and Hazards
Owner / data controller: Consumer Data Research Centre / Geographic Data Service
Age focus / population: Not individual participant data; area-level contextual linkage to cohorts/areas
Access type: Open/public download
Gambling measure summary: Area-level index of access to unhealthy and healthy assets including gambling venues. The Retail Services domain includes gambling outlets alongside fast food, pubs/bars, and vape/tobacco retailers. Covers ~1.7 million postcodes at LSOA/Data Zone level for 2021/22 census boundaries. Not an individual-level gambling survey - provides neighbourhood gambling-environment exposure for contextual linkage.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Built environment, retail environment (gambling outlets, fast food, alcohol/tobacco retail), health services (GPs, pharmacies, hospitals, dentists, leisure centres), green/blue space accessibility, air quality (NO2, PM10, SO2). Four domains combined into composite AHAH score.
Seed/source status: Added at user request as auxiliary/contextual dataset
Notes / uncertainties: AHAH v5 released February 2026. Python toolkit available on GitHub. Higher AHAH scores indicate less healthy environments. Based on Daras et al. (2019) 'Open data on health-related neighbourhood features in Great Britain'. Data sources include NHS Digital, NHS Scotland, DEFRA, Ordnance Survey, OpenStreetMap, and Gambling Commission data. Useful for linking area-level gambling exposure to individual-level cohort data.
Linkage: Joins to any dataset with LSOA codes
Sampling design: Not applicable: area-level geospatial index rather than a survey sample
Data collection mode: Not applicable: compiled from administrative and spatial data sources

Dataset name: 1958 National Child Development Study
Owner / data controller: Centre for Longitudinal Studies, UCL / ESRC
Age focus / population: Born March 1958; sweep 4 (age 23) contains gambling item
Sample size: 17,415 at birth; augmented childhood target sample 18,558; achieved sample at sweep 4 / age 23 = 12,537 cohort members.
Questionnaire URL(s): NCDS Age 23 Annotated Questionnaire Documentation (via UKDS SN 5566)
Access type: UKDS registration; most data freely available
Gambling measure summary: Single gambling participation/frequency item at age 23 (n5919): 'Gambled (including bingo) in past 4 weeks' with 6-point frequency scale.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Verified via CLS metadata and sweep documentation: mental health/depression (Malaise at age 23 and later), smoking and alcohol, family formation and relationships, socioeconomic position/income/housing/employment, education/qualifications, leisure and social participation, physical health. Childhood sweeps add family background, school, cognitive/educational attainment and behaviour/social adjustment.
Notes / uncertainties: Gambling item is in sweep 4 only (age 23, 1981/82). Retrospective adult data: participants aged 23 at gambling measurement. No validated gambling harm scale; single participation/frequency item only. Age 23 achieved sample verified from CLS Age 23 Sweep page.
Source URLs: https://cls.ucl.ac.uk/cls-studies/1958-national-child-development-study/ ; https://cls-data.ucl.ac.uk/explore/variable-search ; https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/ (SN 5566 for sweep 4) ; https://discovery.closer.ac.uk/ ; https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/ ; clsdata@ucl.ac.uk
Linkage: Education and health records via UKDS/CLS
Sampling design: Whole-population birth cohort (all births in one week of 1958; not a random probability sample)
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview plus self-completion questionnaires

Dataset name: 1970 British Cohort Study
Owner / data controller: Centre for Longitudinal Studies, UCL / ESRC
Age focus / population: Born April 1970; sweep 4 (age 15/16) contains gambling items
Sample size: 17,196 at birth including 628 Northern Ireland births not followed in later sweeps; Great Britain cohort 16,568 at birth; achieved sample at sweep 4 / age 16 = 11,622 cohort members.
Catalogue URL: https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/ (SN 3535 for sweep 4 main; SN 8949 for leisure diary)
Questionnaire URL(s): BCS70 Age 16 Survey - Documents G and Q (Student Self-Completion Questionnaires) (via UKDS SN 3535)
Access type: UKDS registration; most data freely available
Gambling measure summary: Direct gambling items at age 15/16: (1) q22.10 'Gone into a betting shop' with frequency scale; (2) gg6.14 'Betting/gambling' as one option in question G6 on what the cohort member would spend extra weekly money on, with tick-all and top-three ranking.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Verified via CLS metadata and sweep documentation: mental health/depression (Malaise first included at age 16), smoking, alcohol and other health behaviours, relationships with family and friends, school/headteacher/teacher data, educational and cognitive assessments, family income/housing/parental circumstances, leisure activities, law/risk-taking, beliefs and aspirations. Later sweeps add employment, income, qualifications, mental/physical health, partnership/family and substance-use data.
Notes / uncertainties: Gambling items at age 15/16 (1986). Direct under-18 gambling data. No validated gambling harm scale. q22.10 is a direct betting-shop participation/frequency item. gg6.14 wording and context verified from CLS/UKDS Document G: spending preference and ranking question.
Source URLs: https://cls.ucl.ac.uk/cls-studies/1970-british-cohort-study/ ; https://cls-data.ucl.ac.uk/explore/variable-search ; https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/ (SN 3535 for sweep 4 main ; SN 8949 for leisure diary) ; https://discovery.closer.ac.uk/ ; https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/ ; clsdata@ucl.ac.uk
Population size note: All GB births, one week of April 1970
Sampling design: Whole-population birth cohort (all births in one week of 1970; not a random probability sample)
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview plus self-completion questionnaires

Dataset name: GambleAware Annual GB Treatment and Support Survey
Owner / data controller: GambleAware
Age focus / population: Adults aged 18+; last two waves (2023, 2024) include retrospective questions about gambling before age 18
Access type: Safeguarded data; application via GeoDS/CDRC or UKDS
Gambling measure summary: PGSI (Problem Gambling Severity Index) with PGSI 1+ (any problems) and PGSI 8+ (problem gambling) thresholds. Gambling participation across product types, frequency, spending. Gambling harms. Demand for and uptake of treatment, support and advice. Affected others (people affected by another person's gambling). Last two waves (2023-2024) include retrospective items on gambling before age 18.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Demographics (age, gender, region, social grade, ethnic group), mental health (linked analysis by Alma Economics 2023), substance use (pre-18 retrospective measures in 2023/2024 waves), socioeconomic position, advertising exposure, stigma, cost-of-living impacts, affected others
Seed/source status: Added from user-provided link to UKDS SN 9536
Notes / uncertainties: Conducted annually by YouGov since 2019; one of the largest gambling harm surveys worldwide. Data weighted by age, gender, UK region, social grade and ethnic group. LSOA-level geographies available for 2019, 2020, 2022 waves. Variables per wave: 962 (2022), 924 (2020), 242 (2019 P1), 736 (2019 P2). Data format CSV. Supplemented by ~30 qualitative interviews/focus groups per wave. Aggregated data tables (Excel) publicly available 2021-2024. Local area data profiles available 2022-2024.
Sampling design: Online panel survey of GB adults (non-probability quota sample, weighted)
Data collection mode: Online self-completion questionnaire

Dataset name: Australian Secondary School Alcohol and Drug Survey
Owner / data controller: Cancer Council Victoria / state health departments
Study design: Cross-sectional school survey (triennial since 1984; gambling module added 2017)
Sample size: 6,377 students from 93 schools (57 Victoria, 36 Queensland) in 2017 gambling module
Access type: Available from corresponding author on reasonable request
Gambling measure summary: DSM-IV-MR-J (12 items, dichotomous yes/no). Gambling participation (ever, past 30 days), types (horse/dog races, sports betting, cards, lotteries, poker machines), modality (online, app, parent-facilitated, venue), problem gambling classification (non-problem, at-risk, problem).
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Demographics (gender, age, SES, geography, language), substance use (alcohol, tobacco, illicit drugs), mental health, money available, school achievement, peer/family gambling, gambling advertising/promotion exposure, venue attendance
Notes / uncertainties: ASSAD has run since 1984 covering alcohol, tobacco and drugs among Australian school students; gambling module first added in 2017. Publication: Freund et al., 2022, J Gambling Studies. DOI: 10.1007/s10899-021-10098-z
Sampling design: Random sample of schools stratified by education sector and state
Data collection mode: Self-completion questionnaire in class

Dataset name: Youth'07 - New Zealand Youth Health and Wellbeing Survey
Owner / data controller: University of Auckland Adolescent Health Research Group
Access type: Published open access; data access route unclear
Gambling measure summary: Custom gambling items: past-year gambling, gambling activities (Lotto, pokies, casino, internet, TAB betting), frequency, money spent weekly, time spent daily, reasons for gambling (13 options including 'can't stop', 'feel better about myself'). No standard named instrument (PGSI/SOGS-RA) used.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Depression (Reynolds Adolescent Depression Scale-Short Form), wellbeing (WHO-5), social connectedness (family, friends, school), weekly alcohol use, weekly income, demographics (age, sex, ethnicity), neighbourhood deprivation
Notes / uncertainties: Data collected in 2007. Publication: Rossen et al., 2016, Asian J Gambling Issues Public Health. DOI: 10.1186/s40405-016-0017-9. Part of the Youth2000 survey series (Youth2000, Youth'07, Youth'12).
Sampling design: Nationally representative random sample of secondary schools and students
Data collection mode: Self-completion questionnaire on handheld multimedia devices

Dataset name: Finnish School Health Promotion Study
Owner / data controller: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
Access type: Data available from THL with restrictions; not publicly available but accessible upon request
Gambling measure summary: Weekly gambling frequency ('How often do you gamble?' with frequency categories: 1-2, 3-5, 6-7 days per week).
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Substance use (heavy episodic drinking, daily smoking, lifetime drug use), sports activity, school orientation, health perception, life satisfaction, peer relationships (close friendships), family communication, financial situation, youth origin/migration status
Notes / uncertainties: Very large sample. Publication: Raitasalo et al., 2024, J Gambling Studies. DOI: 10.1007/s10899-024-10321-7. Focus on youth origin/migration as risk factor. See also AHLS (Adolescent Health and Lifestyle Survey) for complementary Finnish data.
Sampling design: Whole-population school survey (students in relevant grades across Finland; not a random probability sample)
Data collection mode: Online self-completion questionnaire in class

Dataset name: Growing Up in Australia: Longitudinal Study of Australian Children
Owner / data controller: Australian Institute of Family Studies (AIFS) / Department of Social Services
Study design: Nationally representative longitudinal cohort (two cohorts recruited 2004; surveyed roughly every two years)
Age focus / population: Two cohorts followed from infancy; young-person gambling module ages 16-24, plus Parent 1 gambling module
Sample size: B cohort n=5,107 (aged 0-1 in 2004); K cohort n=4,983 (aged 4-5 in 2004); Wave 10 (2023-24) retained approx 2,335 K and 2,498 B families
Access type: Free via Australian Data Archive (ADA) Dataverse after registration and signed confidentiality deed; non-Australian researchers receive General Release only (Restricted Release requires Australian collaborators)
Gambling measure summary: PGSI and gambling participation for young people: K cohort at Wave 7 (2016, 16-17), Wave 8 (2018, 18-19), Wave 9C2 (2021, 20-22) and Wave 10 (2023-24, 23-24); B cohort at Wave 9C2 (16-18) and Wave 10 (19-20). Both cohorts answered a single 'did you gamble during COVID restrictions' item at Wave 9C1 (2020). Parent 1 completed the full gambling module twice: Wave 7 (participation, simulated gambling, own and family lifetime problem gambling, PGSI) and Wave 9C1 (participation, mode, PGSI). From Wave 5, Parent 1 was also asked whether the family used or needed problem-gambling support services (repeated to Wave 9C2).
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental health and wellbeing, substance use, family and household context, peer relationships, school and education, socioeconomic position and demographics, digital/technology use
Notes / uncertainties: Two cohorts (B, aged 0-1; K, aged 4-5) recruited 2004; 10 main waves (Wave 9 was two short COVID surveys, 9C1 2020 and 9C2 2021). Attrition substantial by Wave 10. Wave 10 data released October 2025. Study links to administrative databases with participant consent.
Population size: approx 10,090 children at recruitment (B n=5,107; K n=4,983)
Population size note: Wave 10 (2023-24) retained approx 2,335 K and 2,498 B families
Years covered: 2016, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2023-2024 (young-person gambling module Waves 7-10; Parent 1 module Waves 5-9)
Linkage: Administrative data linkage with participant consent
Sampling design: Two-stage random probability sample (postcodes then children) designed to be nationally representative
Data collection mode: Face-to-face home interview (CAPI) plus self-completion; COVID Waves 9C1/9C2 conducted online/by telephone

Dataset name: Young Persons' Behaviour and Attitudes Survey
Owner / data controller: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency (NISRA)
Study design: Cross-sectional school-based survey of post-primary pupils (roughly every three years since 2000; gambling module in the 2022 wave only)
Sample size: 2022 survey: 7,498 pupils total; 3,772 completed the gambling module (Version B questionnaire)
Access type: Aggregate results published by NISRA/Department of Health; individual-level microdata available via the UK Data Service (SN 9195). Contact csu@nisra.gov.uk (NISRA Central Survey Unit)
Gambling measure summary: 2022 gambling module (Version B questionnaire): gambling participation across 8 activity types (past 12 months); spending on in-game items/loot boxes and betting with in-game items (skins betting); reasons for gambling; gambling to escape problems; and perceived frequency and emotional impact of parental/family gambling. No validated harm screen was used.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Family/peer gambling, digital and technology use (in-game items, loot boxes, skins betting), mental health and wellbeing, substance use, socioeconomic position and demographics (school year, gender)
Notes / uncertainties: Only the 2022 wave includes a gambling module. No validated harm screen. The next publication covering 2025 YPBAS findings is expected in late 2026. Data access through the UK Data Service; contact csu@nisra.gov.uk.
Population size: approx 7,500 pupils (2022); 3,772 completed the gambling module
Population size note: Version B subsample answered the gambling questions
Sampling design: School-based sample of post-primary schools and pupils (gambling module administered to the Version B subsample)
Data collection mode: Self-completion questionnaire in school

Dataset name: OxWell Student Survey
Owner / data controller: University of Oxford (Department of Psychiatry)
Study design: Repeated cross-sectional school survey (waves 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023, 2025; gambling items in 2019-2021 only)
Age focus / population: Pupils aged 8-18 (school Years 4-13 incl. FE colleges); gambling items asked of older pupils only
Sample size: Total sample varies by year (2019: approx 4,000; 2020: approx 19,000; 2021: approx 31,000); gambling subsamples are smaller (older year groups only)
Access type: Free for researchers; access via the data access form on the Brainwaves Hub portal (DPUK). Contact oxwell@psych.ox.ac.uk or PI Mina Fazel (mina.fazel@psych.ox.ac.uk)
Gambling measure summary: Gambling items appear only in 2019-2021 and only for older pupils, with no validated harm screen. 2019: past-12-month participation in 7 gambling activities (Year 12 only). 2020: Years 12-13 only, participation plus online gambling (ever tried; frequency of real-money use). 2021: extended to Years 8-13, asking only about ever trying online gambling, using real money, and owing money (not to family). Gambling was dropped from 2023 onwards.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental health and wellbeing, digital and technology use (online gambling/gaming), socioeconomic position and demographics, family context
Notes / uncertainties: Five waves (2019, 2020, 2021, 2023, 2025); geographical coverage varies across surveys, with Oxfordshire County included in every wave. Gambling variables only 2019-2021 and only for older pupils; no validated harm screen. Variable guides available on the OSF website.
Population size: approx 4,000 (2019) to approx 31,000 (2021) pupils per wave
Population size note: Gambling subsamples smaller (older year groups only)
Sampling design: Opt-in school sample; geographical coverage varies by wave (Oxfordshire included every wave); not a random probability sample
Data collection mode: Online self-completion questionnaire in school

Dataset name: UK Biobank gambling-adjacent questionnaire and linked clinical records
Owner / data controller: UK Biobank
Study design: Prospective volunteer cohort with questionnaires and linked health records
Access type: UK Biobank approved research application
Gambling measure summary: Gambling-specific hospital and GP clinical codes; a non-specific behavioural-addiction questionnaire branch in which gambling is named only as an example
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Extensive health, mental health, substance, socioeconomic, genetic and linked-record factors
Screening status: Include with caveat only if linked clinical records are in scope
Notes / uncertainties: Category 141 of the public UK Biobank Data Showcase was reviewed in full: no field isolates gambling. The addiction-branch fields are a non-specific proxy and the only gambling-specific content is the linked ICD-10 and primary-care code list.
Population size note: Approximately 500,000 participants recruited overall. Showcase counts at review: 157,130 for field 20401, 9,361 for 20431, and 2,236 for 20552 and 20432.
Sampling design: Volunteer prospective cohort recruited at ages 40-69 through invitations based on NHS patient registers near 22 assessment centres
Data collection mode: Baseline touchscreen questionnaire, nurse interview, physical measures and biosamples; online follow-up questionnaire; linked health records

Dataset name: Smoking and Alcohol Toolkit Studies: October 2022 GB gambling module
Owner / data controller: University College London / Smoking and Alcohol Toolkit Studies
Study design: Repeated cross-sectional surveillance survey; one-off gambling pilot module
Age focus / population: Adults aged 18+ living in Great Britain
Access type: Study-managed request
Gambling measure summary: Sixteen past-year activities, full PGSI, and weekly gambling expenditure
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Smoking and AUDIT-C alcohol risk; demographics and socioeconomic variables
Notes / uncertainties: One-off October 2022 module; activity-to-gmb1* mapping and spend source ID require controlled codebook
Sampling design: Hybrid random-location and quota sampling
Data collection mode: Telephone interview

Dataset name: National Gambling Support Network Data Reporting Framework, 2015-2026
Owner / data controller: GambleAware / commissioned NGSN providers; UK Data Service distributor
Study design: Longitudinal treatment-service administrative records in linked relational tables
Age focus / population: Adults aged 18+ accessing NGSN treatment or support
Questionnaire URL(s): Data Reporting Framework specifications in UKDS deposit
Access type: UK Data Service safeguarded access
Gambling measure summary: PGSI score recorded at every appointment; ten gambling activity fields; gambling history covering onset age, early big win, time and money spent, debt, job loss and relationship loss; self-exclusion tool use; CORE-10 and treatment outcome measures
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: CORE-10 psychological distress; demographics; treatment engagement and self-exclusion
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the eleven released UK Data Service data dictionaries (SN 9537) across two deposits: 2015-2021 (activities, appointments, history, person, referrals) and 2021-2026 (appointments, careplan, history, modality, person, referrals). Field codes are scoped to a table and a deposit - G3 is a gambling activity in the 2015-2021 activities table, length of time gambling in the 2015-2021 history table, and job loss in the 2021-2026 history table - so table and period must always be carried with the code. Service records, not survey responses.
Linkage: Relational person, referral, gambling history/activity, appointment, care plan and modality tables
Sampling design: Census/collection of participating treatment-provider activity, subject to provider coverage
Data collection mode: Provider administrative reporting

Dataset name: Canadian Community Health Survey: gambling modules and rapid responses
Owner / data controller: Statistics Canada
Study design: Repeated cross-sectional national health survey with optional and rapid-response gambling modules
Age focus / population: Household population aged 12+ or 15+ depending cycle; adult subsamples available
Access type: Research Data Centre controlled access to detailed master files
Gambling measure summary: Product and frequency items, online/in-person mode, full PGSI, derived severity variables
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental and physical health, alcohol, smoking, socioeconomic position, household and inequality variables
Notes / uncertainties: Create separate rows by cycle; 2025 Rapid Response fields pending documentation
Population size: 2018 final CCHS n=26,648; gambling module analytic n=24,983
Population size note: 2018 final sample n=26,648; gambling module n=24,983 age 15+. Other cycle counts must be retained by source file.
Sampling design: Cross-sectional probability household survey
Data collection mode: Computer-assisted interview; cycle-specific

Dataset name: Household, Income and Labour Dynamics in Australia Survey
Owner / data controller: Australian Government Department of Social Services; Melbourne Institute study manager
Age focus / population: All household members aged 15+; adult subsamples available
Codebook / variable URL(s): HILDA Release 22 data dictionary in approved release
Access type: Approved researcher access through ADA under confidentiality deed
Gambling measure summary: Product-specific typical monthly expenditure and full PGSI in waves 15, 18 and 22
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Income, wealth, hardship, work, education, family, mental/physical health, wellbeing and substance use
Notes / uncertainties: Confirm exact released field names from Wave 15/18/22 dictionaries
Population size: Wave 15 n=17,605 interviews; wave 18 n=17,434; wave 22 n=15,954. Wave 15 gambling module n=15,245.
Sampling design: National household probability panel with Wave 11 top-up
Data collection mode: Interview plus self-completion questionnaire

Dataset name: Finnish Gambling Surveys, 2007-2023
Owner / data controller: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare; Statistics Finland collector; Finnish Social Science Data Archive distributor
Age focus / population: Household population aged 15-74; adult subsamples available
Access type: FSD registration for earlier waves; depositor permission for 2023
Gambling measure summary: Products, frequency, mode and spend; PGSI; SOGS (2015 and 2019); attitudes; a six-domain gambling harms battery (financial, work/study, health, emotional, relationship, other); affected-other harms; digital gaming, loot boxes and gaming-disorder items; MHI-5; AUDIT-C
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: ATGS-8, MHI-5, AUDIT-C, GAS-7, family/friends, advertising, income, education, work and inequalities
Notes / uncertainties: Indexed variables cover the 2011, 2015 and 2019 waves, whose released column names are confirmed in the FSD variable catalogue. The 2023 wave (FSD3917) is documented here from its questionnaire only: 63 items covering gambling attitudes (1-7), participation, mode and spend (8-21), motives and problem perception (22-24), a six-domain harms battery (27-34), affected-other harms (35-37), digital gaming and loot boxes (38-48), health, loneliness and MHI-5 (49-52), AUDIT-C and alcohol use while gambling (53-56), and demographics (57-63). The questionnaire numbers items sequentially and carries no variable identifiers, so no 2023 column names are recorded; those need the FSD3917 variable catalogue, which requires depositor permission.
Sampling design: Systematic random population-register samples
Data collection mode: CATI through 2019; web/postal plus CATI mode study in 2023

Dataset name: Gambling Commission Gambling Behaviour Quarterly Telephone Survey, 2016-2022
Owner / data controller: Gambling Commission
Study design: Repeated cross-sectional quarterly telephone survey; annual UKDS files
Access type: UK Data Service registration
Gambling measure summary: Past-four-week participation and frequency; three-item PGSI mini-screen; ATGS-8
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Gambling attitudes and sociodemographic inequalities
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the released UK Data Service data dictionaries for all seven years: 2016 (SN 9091), 2017 (SN 9103), 2018 (SN 9104), 2019 (SN 9105), 2020 (SN 9106), 2021 (SN 9107) and 2022 (SN 9113). The series is strictly additive - no variable is dropped in any year. The wave identifier is capitalised as "Wave" in the 2020 dictionary only. Sample sizes are not stated in the dictionaries themselves.
Population size note: Annual totals pooled across four quarterly waves per year.
Sampling design: Random digit dialling with quotas and weighting
Data collection mode: CATI

Dataset name: 2019 ACT Gambling Prevalence Survey
Owner / data controller: Australian National University Centre for Gambling Research / ACT Gambling and Racing Commission
Access type: ADA Request Access for restricted ZIP
Gambling measure summary: Full nine-item PGSI with released raw score and category; product-level participation, frequency and expenditure; gambling harms; affected-other harms; help-seeking and information sources; video-game and loot-box purchasing
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Attitudes, help seeking, wellbeing, financial hardship and demographics
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the released ADA data dictionary for the SRC2231 data file. Access requires an ADA Dataverse account and an approved request.
Sampling design: Survey design documented in report; verify detailed frame in package
Data collection mode: CATI

Dataset name: National Comorbidity Survey Replication
Owner / data controller: Harvard Medical School / University of Michigan; ICPSR distributor
Age focus / population: US household adults aged 18+; gambling in Part II subsample
Access type: ICPSR public-use/registration; restricted agreement for detailed geography
Gambling measure summary: Full CIDI DSM-IV pathological gambling module: eleven lifetime activity-type items, onset and frequency, largest single loss and net position, the ten DSM-IV criterion items with consequence, persistence and recency probes, gambling motives, dissociation items, and help-seeking and treatment history
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Full psychiatric CIDI modules, substance use, personality, childhood adversity, finances, employment, marriage and social networks
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the CPES public-use crosswalk (BLGAMBLING sheet), which maps CPES V-numbers to released field names in each constituent survey. All 84 gambling fields are present in NCS-R; five (GM1, GM2, GM4, GM5, GM6) are also fielded in NSAL and none in NLAAS, so the module is effectively NCS-R only.
Sampling design: National multistage clustered area probability sample
Data collection mode: Computer-assisted personal interview

Dataset name: Liquor, Gambling and Cannabis in Manitoba Survey II, 2022
Owner / data controller: Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba / GREO distributor
Access type: Borealis/GREO file request; verify file licence
Gambling measure summary: Thirteen gambling participation frequency items by product, COVID-19 impact on gambling frequency, estimated monthly gambling spend, and gambling spending-limit behaviours. No problem gambling severity screen is included.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Alcohol, cannabis, attitudes and responsible-gambling limits
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the released LGCM II (2022) codebook. The survey carries no PGSI, CPGI or other problem gambling severity screen - gambling content is participation, spend and spending-limit behaviour only. Substance-use content is extensive: the full ten-item AUDIT, drinking motives, protective drinking strategies, and parallel cannabis use, motive and strategy blocks. Survey fielded in 2022; codebook published September 2025. Catalogue ID renamed from MANITOBA_LGCS_II_2025, which took its year from the codebook publication date rather than the fieldwork year.

Dataset name: Quinte Longitudinal Study of Gambling and Problem Gambling
Owner / data controller: Gambling Research Exchange Ontario / original QLS investigators
Age focus / population: Adults approximately 18-90 in the Quinte region
Questionnaire URL(s): Questionnaires/user manual in controlled Dataverse package
Access type: GREO restricted-data request and Terms of Use
Gambling measure summary: CPGI/PGSI items with total and category, NODS and PPGM scored in parallel on the same items, past-year and lifetime participation by product, gambling motivation, fallacies and attitudes
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Psychiatric and substance disorders, stress, personality/impulsivity, family/social functioning, employment and income
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the released QLS response-data codebooks for all five assessments. The same problem gambling items are scored three ways - CPGI, NODS and PPGM - using _NODS and _PPGM suffixed copies, which makes the study unusually useful for instrument comparison. Assessment 2 fields carry an A2_ prefix.
Sampling design: RDD general-population cohort plus at-risk oversample
Data collection mode: Telephone/online modes documented in user manual

Dataset name: Leisure, Lifestyle and Lifecycle Project
Owner / data controller: Alberta Gambling Research Institute investigators / GREO Dataverse
Age focus / population: Adult cohorts aged 18-20, 23-25, 43-45 and 63-65; separate adolescent file
Questionnaire URL(s): User manual and questionnaires in Dataverse package
Access type: GREO restricted-data request and Terms of Use
Gambling measure summary: CPGI participation and severity blocks with derived totals and 5+ categories, PPGM subscales, internet gambling module, across adolescent and adult cohorts
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental/physical health, personality, coping, ADHD, eating/substance disorders, religiosity and social support
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the nine released LLLP response-data codebooks: adolescent waves 1-4, adult waves 1-4, and the combined wave 5. Note that "cpgi" names the questionnaire block in this study, not the scored instrument - most cpgi-prefixed fields are participation items, so only derived CPGI totals, categories and PPGM subscales carry a named measure here.
Sampling design: Predominantly RDD plus targeted supplementary recruitment
Data collection mode: Survey modes documented in user manual

Dataset name: AGRI National Project Online Panel Study
Owner / data controller: Alberta Gambling Research Institute investigators / GREO
Study design: Two-wave national online panel of monthly gamblers
Age focus / population: Canadian adults aged 18+ who gambled at least monthly
Questionnaire URL(s): User manual and questionnaires in controlled package
Access type: GREO restricted-data request
Gambling measure summary: Full PGSI item set with categories, PPGM items and subscales, gambling fallacies, motives, attitudes, advertising exposure, family history and derived spend and time measures
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Fallacies, family history, mental health, personality, behavioural addictions, substance use and PTSD
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the released baseline and follow-up codebooks. Baseline n=10,199.

Dataset name: English Longitudinal Study of Ageing - gambling winnings proxy
Owner / data controller: ELSA study team / UK Data Service distributor
Access type: UKDS registered/special-licence access
Gambling measure summary: One response option (code 7) inside a bundled income-receipt item covering football pools, national lottery or other gambling winnings. No separable amount, participation, frequency or harm measure.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Rich ageing, health, wealth, work, family and wellbeing measures
Screening status: Include with caveat as proxy only
Notes / uncertainties: Released columns Iapk01-Iapk05 confirmed at pages 167-168 of the Wave 1 documentation. Recorded as a proxy so the negative result is documented: ELSA has been checked and carries no gambling module. UK Data Service SN 5050 was at its 50th release in July 2026.

Dataset name: Gaming and Betting Study: Survey of Loyalty Card Customers, Waves 1 and 2, 2014-2016
Owner / data controller: NatCen Social Research for GambleAware (formerly the Responsible Gambling Trust); UK Data Service distributor
Study design: Two-wave longitudinal survey of bookmaker loyalty card holders
Age focus / population: Adults holding a Ladbrokes, William Hill or Paddy Power loyalty card who had played machines in a bookmakers
Access type: UK Data Service End User Licence
Gambling measure summary: Full nine-item PGSI at both waves with released score, grouped score and problem-gambling classification; past-4-week participation and frequency across 19 products and channels; derived weekly, daily and days-per-product intensity measures; gambling harm items covering arguments, failing to meet expectations and the household going without; machine-play limit setting and operator interventions; motives for machine play and reasons gambling increased or decreased between waves
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Impulsivity (BIS), rational-experiential thinking style, cognitive reflection, ONS4 wellbeing, general health, life events, household composition, education, income, deprivation and demographics
Seed/source status: Identified from the Harmony gambling dataset list and screened against public documentation
Notes / uncertainties: Variable list built from the released UK Data Service user guide, which prints every variable name and label for the deposited file RGT1416.sav. The linked loyalty-card machine-play records analysed in the original reports are NOT part of the deposit. Respondents are loyalty card holders, not a general population sample, so prevalence estimates are not generalisable. The Wave 1 report PDF has been removed from the GambleAware site; the Wave 2 report remains live.
Population size: n=4,727 at Wave 1; n=1,552 in the released longitudinal file
Population size note: Wave 1 achieved 4,727 interviews of which 4,001 consented to loyalty-card linkage; Wave 2 achieved 1,561 full interviews and the deposited file holds the 1,552 cases productive at both waves
Linkage: Loyalty-card machine-play records were linked for the original analysis but are not included in the deposit
Sampling design: Random probability sample of 27,565 loyalty card holders drawn from Ladbrokes, William Hill and Paddy Power industry registers; Wave 2 followed up Wave 1 respondents who agreed to recontact
Data collection mode: Web or telephone at Wave 1; telephone (CATI) at Wave 2

Dataset name: Cambridge Study in Delinquent Development, 1961-1981
Owner / data controller: David P. Farrington, University of Cambridge Institute of Criminology; ICPSR/NACJD distributor
Study design: Prospective longitudinal cohort with repeated interviews, parent, teacher and peer ratings, and criminal-record searches
Age focus / population: 411 males from a working-class area of South London, born around 1953 and followed from age 8
Access type: ICPSR/NACJD download with a free account
Gambling measure summary: Betting participation by product (football pools, horses, dogs, cards) and amount bet per month at the age 18-19 interview; most won and most lost in a week; a derived three-level gambling classification; weekly betting expenditure at age 21-22; retrospective items on spending 1 pound or more a week on gambling under age 16 at the age 14-15 and 16-17 interviews; and a behavioural measure in which respondents were offered a double-or-nothing coin toss for part of their interview fee
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Delinquency and convictions, family background, parenting, school attainment, IQ, personality, employment, drinking, smoking and drug use across the full cohort codebook
Seed/source status: Identified from the Catalogue of Mental Health Measures gambling topic and screened against the public NACJD codebook
Notes / uncertainties: Only the gambling variables are catalogued here; the full released file holds 876 variables across 14 card images and the public codebook is a scanned document, so variable numbers should be checked against the ICPSR data file before analysis. Amounts are in pre-decimal and 1970s pounds. The dataset covers the study period to 1981; later follow-ups at ages 32 and 48 are not in this deposit.
Population size note: 389 of the original 411 were interviewed at age 18-19
Linkage: Criminal Record Office searches linked for cohort members and their families
Sampling design: All boys aged 8-9 on the registers of six state primary schools in a working-class area of South London
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interviews with the boys and their parents, teacher and peer questionnaires, and record searches

Dataset name: West of Scotland Twenty-07 Study: Health in the Community
Owner / data controller: MRC/CSO Social and Public Health Sciences Unit, University of Glasgow
Study design: Three-cohort longitudinal study of people born around 1932, 1952 and 1972, followed over five waves from 1987/88 to 2007/08
Age focus / population: Regional sample from the Central Clydeside Conurbation plus a localities sample from two Glasgow areas
Access type: Application to the study team
Gambling measure summary: Three frequency items inside the Wave 4 leisure grid: doing the lottery or scratchcards, betting on horses, dogs or sports matches, and gambling on cards, fruit machines or bingo. Eight-point scale from every day to never.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Employment and unemployment history, mental health, physical health, health behaviours, area deprivation, social support, youth style and delinquency
Seed/source status: Identified from the Catalogue of Mental Health Measures gambling topic and screened against the public Wave 4 questionnaire
Notes / uncertainties: The gambling items are asked of the 1970s cohort only. The Wave 4 questionnaire routes the 1930s and 1950s cohorts past Q139 to Q143. A search of the public Wave 5 questionnaire found no gambling item. Only the three gambling variables are catalogued here; the study holds a much larger variable set.
Population size: About 4,510 at baseline across the three cohorts
Population size note: At Wave 4 the 1970s cohort was aged about 28 and had 1% cumulative mortality; attrition figures are in the cohort profile
Linkage: Health record linkage available under the study's own governance
Sampling design: Two-stage stratified random regional sample plus a localities sample
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview

Dataset name: Mental Health of Children and Young People in England
Owner / data controller: NHS England (formerly NHS Digital), with the Office for National Statistics, National Centre for Social Research and the University of Cambridge
Study design: National probability survey with follow-up waves
Age focus / population: Children and young people in England, with follow-up waves in 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023
Access type: UK Data Service; published statistics are open
Gambling measure summary: One item on the number of days in the past 7 days on which the respondent gambled money online, asked inside an activities grid. A topcoded derived version exists for 2020.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Mental health diagnoses, wellbeing, sleep, loneliness, social media use, substance use, eating problems and family circumstances
Seed/source status: Identified from the Catalogue of Mental Health Measures gambling topic and screened against the published questionnaire materials
Notes / uncertainties: This is a single online-gambling frequency item, not a problem-gambling screen. Age universes differ by year: young people 17-22 in 2020, 17-23 in 2021, 17-24 in 2022 and 17-25 in 2023, with children aged 11-16 also asked in 2022 and 2023. The item is not in the 2017 baseline. The 2021 and 2022 questionnaires print only the grid name, not the per-item column name, so only the 2020 and 2023 names are recorded here.
Population size note: Follow-up samples vary by year; see the statistical release for each wave
Linkage: Consent sought for linkage to NHS, education and ONS records
Sampling design: Follow-up of the 2017 probability sample
Data collection mode: Online or telephone

Dataset name: British Household Panel Survey - gambling winnings proxy
Owner / data controller: Institute for Social and Economic Research, University of Essex; UK Data Service distributor
Study design: Annual household panel, 1991 to 2008, subsequently absorbed into Understanding Society
Access type: UK Data Service End User Licence
Gambling measure summary: PROXY ONLY. Whether the respondent received a payment from a win on the football pools, national lottery or other form of gambling since 1 September of the previous year, and the amount received. There is no participation, frequency, stake, loss, product, screen or harm item.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Income, employment, housing, household composition, physical and mental health across the full panel
Seed/source status: Identified from the Catalogue of Mental Health Measures gambling topic and screened against the public wave questionnaires
Screening status: Include as a labelled proxy only
Notes / uncertainties: Recorded as a proxy on the same basis as the ELSA and UK Biobank records: it identifies people who received winnings, not people who gambled, and non-gamblers and unsuccessful gamblers are indistinguishable. Published BHPS research states this limitation explicitly. Waves 17 and 18 are catalogued because their questionnaires were verified directly; the item is reported across waves 7 to 18 (1997-2009) using the standard BHPS wave-letter prefix, and those names have not been verified here. Understanding Society is catalogued separately as USOC.
Years covered: 1997-2009 for the winnings item; waves 17 and 18 verified here
Sampling design: Nationally representative household panel with country boosts
Data collection mode: Face-to-face interview

Dataset name: Health and Wellbeing Cohort Study (King's Centre for Military Health Research)
Owner / data controller: King's Centre for Military Health Research, King's College London
Study design: Four-phase cohort study of UK Armed Forces personnel from the Iraq and Afghanistan era
Age focus / population: Serving and ex-serving UK Armed Forces personnel, Regulars and Reservists
Access type: Project proposal to the study team
Gambling measure summary: Problem Gambling Severity Index, added at Phase 4 and listed as measure 13 in the published protocol with the conventional cut-off of 8 or more. Released column names are not public.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: PTSD and complex PTSD, common mental disorders, alcohol (AUDIT), illicit drug use (DUDIT), suicidal ideation and self-harm, anger, aggression, traumatic brain injury, loneliness, social support, relationship quality and cognitive decline
Seed/source status: Identified from the Catalogue of Mental Health Measures gambling topic and screened against the public Phase 4 protocol
Screening status: Include - study level only, pending item metadata
Notes / uncertainties: Catalogued at study level. The PGSI is named in the Phase 4 protocol but no questionnaire, codebook or released column names are public, so no variable names are recorded. Gambling measurement is Phase 4 only; earlier phases (2004-06, 2007-09, 2014-16) are not established as carrying gambling items.
Population size: N=7,608 invited at Phase 4 from Phase 3 responders who consented to recontact
Population size note: Phase 4 is a legacy cohort with no replenishment sample
Linkage: Not stated in the public protocol
Sampling design: Follow-up of the Phase 3 cohort, originally a random sample of UK service personnel
Data collection mode: Online or paper questionnaire

Dataset name: Genetic Links to Anxiety and Depression Study
Owner / data controller: King's College London / NIHR BioResource
Study design: Volunteer recontactable cohort with genetic and questionnaire data
Age focus / population: Participants aged 16 and over with lifetime anxiety or depression, recruited from September 2018
Access type: Application to the NIHR BioResource / GLAD team
Gambling measure summary: An optional follow-up questionnaire described in the published cohort profile as asking detailed questions about gambling. The instrument, items, reference period and column names are not public.
Key risk/protective domains confirmed: Anxiety and depression phenotypes, trauma and PTSD, OCD, eating disorders, substance use, sleep, life events and genetic data
Seed/source status: Identified from the Catalogue of Mental Health Measures gambling topic and screened against the published cohort profile
Screening status: Include - study level only, pending item metadata
Notes / uncertainties: Catalogued at study level. The cohort profile confirms a gambling questionnaire exists but publishes nothing below that. GLAD content drew on the Australian Genetics of Depression Study, which has a public games and gambling module, but that wording and those variable names must not be assumed to apply here.
Population size note: The number completing the optional gambling questionnaire is not published
Linkage: Genetic data and NIHR BioResource recontact
Sampling design: Self-selected volunteers recruited through a national media campaign
Data collection mode: Online questionnaire with a saliva kit
